title: Octagons and hexagons of the Comares dado (Alhambra)
subtitle: Comares dado, Alhambra

construction.note: The finished design was read from Brian Wichmann’s J43A drawing. We devised the construction using a band size obtained from a line through a cell corner. The reference does not supply this sequence of steps.
construction.changes: The app’s compass operations, step order and named intersections are our reconstruction. Recorded drawing and photo comparisons assess the finished line structure, not whether these were the historical construction steps.

given.A: Halfway from O to the next octagon.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A.

Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through A. Draw a vertical line through B. Draw a horizontal line through C. Draw a horizontal line through D. These four lines make the square cell, with corners E, F, G and H.
Draw a straight line through O and E. It crosses the circle at R. Draw a straight line through F and R. It crosses the right side of the cell at X1.
Draw a circle with centre E through X1. It crosses the top of the cell at X2. Draw a straight line through X1 and X2. This line is a side of the small square at E.

Draw a vertical line through X2. Draw a horizontal line through X1. Draw a line through X1 parallel to line OE. Draw a line through X2 parallel to line OE. These are sides of the octagon, the long hexagons and the small squares.

Draw a straight line through P1 and P2. P1 is where the vertical line through X2 crosses the lower slanting line. P2 is where the horizontal line through X1 crosses the upper one. This line is a slanting side of the octagon.
Turn these six lines round O by 90°, three times. This copies them to the other corners of the cell.
Mark each point where the outline of the pattern turns.
Join E, F, G and H to mark the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink the octagon at O. Ink the lines from the octagon out to the sides of the cell, and across each corner.

parts.text: Ink the octagon: from P1 through P2, P3 and on round the octagon, back to P1. Its corners are P1 to P8.
Ink from P1 to X1, from X1 to X2, and from X2 to P2. These lines close the small square at E.
Ink the same three lines at F, G and H. Tick “Also ink the copies round the centre” to ink them all at once.

pattern.text: Put copies of the square cell side by side. Octagons sit on the grid, with a long hexagon between each two. Five small squares make a cross where four cells touch.
